overview: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean. Its capital and largest city is Havana. Cuba was a Spanish colony until 1898. After a revolution in 1959 led by Fidel Castro, it became a communist state, which it remains today. Cuba is known around the world for its music, cigars and classic old cars.

geography.text: Cuba is long and narrow, stretching more than 1,000 kilometres from east to west, and is surrounded by thousands of smaller islands and cays. Most of the land is flat or gently rolling and used for farming, especially sugar cane and tobacco. The highest mountains, the Sierra Maestra, are in the south-east. Cuba lies only about 150 kilometres south of Florida.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Tropical and warm, with a rainy season from May to October and a risk of hurricanes.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: The bee hummingbird, the smallest bird in the world, and the Cuban crocodile.

history.text: Spain ruled Cuba for almost 400 years, and its sugar plantations relied on enslaved Africans. After wars of independence and US intervention in 1898, Cuba became a republic in 1902. Fidel Castro's revolution in 1959 created a communist state, and the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962 brought the world close to nuclear war.

events.title: Columbus arrives
events.text: Columbus lands on Cuba on his first voyage.

events.title: Spanish–American War
events.text: Spain loses Cuba after US intervention.

events.title: Bay of Pigs
events.text: A US-backed invasion by Cuban exiles fails.

events.title: Missile Crisis
events.text: Soviet missiles in Cuba bring the superpowers to the brink of war.

government.text: Cuba is a one-party communist state. The Communist Party of Cuba is the only legal party. The National Assembly elects the President, and the Prime Minister runs the government. Fidel Castro led the country from 1959 to 2008, followed by his brother Raúl until 2018.

economy.text: Most of Cuba's economy is controlled by the state. Tourism, nickel mining, cigars, rum and the export of doctors to other countries bring in money. A US trade embargo has been in place since the early 1960s, and shortages of food, fuel and electricity have caused hardship.

culture.text: Cuban music, from son and salsa to the rumba, has spread across the world, and rumba is listed by UNESCO. Old Havana is full of colonial buildings and classic 1950s American cars. Cuban cigars are among the most famous in the world.

items.title: Old Havana
items.text: A colonial city centre listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Classic cars
items.text: American cars from the 1950s still drive the streets.

items.title: Buena Vista Social Club
items.text: A 1997 album that made Cuban son music famous worldwide.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Ropa vieja, shredded beef stew, with rice and black beans.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Son, salsa, rumba and the Buena Vista Social Club; Cuban ballet is world-class.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: In Havana's streets, classic 1950s cars, dominoes and music are part of daily life.

sport.text: Baseball is Cuba's national sport, and Cuba has won Olympic gold three times. Boxing has brought it dozens of Olympic gold medals, and athletes such as the high jumper Javier Sotomayor, who still holds the world record set in 1993, are national heroes.

items.title: Boxing
items.text: Cuba has won more than 40 Olympic boxing golds.

items.title: Javier Sotomayor
items.text: Set the high jump world record of 2.45 m in 1993.

items.title: Mijaín López
items.text: The first athlete to win the same individual Olympic event five times, in wrestling.

didYouKnow: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean.
The bee hummingbird, found in Cuba, is the smallest bird in the world.
